newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Korea Heavy in Sri Lanka steel mill privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Korea Heavy in Sri Lanka steel mill privatisation.

text.p: Sri Lanka said it sold 90 percent of Ceylon Steel Corporation to Korea Heavy Industries and Construction Co Ltd (Hanjung) for $15 million.

"In addition to the purchase price, Korea Heavy will spend a further $10 million on plant modernisation," a spokeswoman for the Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), which oversees privatisation of state firms, told Reuters.

An executive from Korea Heavy told Reuters in September that Ceylon Steel would be a foothold for Korea Heavy's business operations in Sri Lanka, which would include power generation and oil refining.
Executive managing director of the company Shin Sang-hong said the company would upgrade Ceylon Steel, but also look at investing in a new mill in a harbour city he declined to name.
Ceylon Steel is on 72 ha of land in a Colombo suburb.
Under a long-term investment plan, Korea Heavy hopes to build a power plant at a cost of $150 million and an oil refinery at a cost of $350 million, Shin said.
The privatisation of Ceylon Steel Corporation formed part of government plans to restructure loss-making state ventures.
"In line with the privatisation formula, Ceylon Steel's 1,400-strong workforce will get 93 million rupees worth of shares free of charge," said the spokeswoman.
If employees want to sell their shares, Korea Heavy has said it is prepared to buy, she said.
